title: Parse a CSV line
instructorPromptText: Write a C function `int parse_csv(const char *line, char fields[][100], int max_fields)` that parses a single CSV line into a 2D character array of fields. The function must handle fields enclosed in double quotes that contain commas and return the total fields parsed.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program maintain a state variable (e.g. `in_quotes`) to track whether the current character is inside double quotes?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Handling commas inside quotes requires a state machine approach. Simple tokenizers like `strtok` will fail.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program explicitly null-terminate (`\0`) each field copied into the 2D array?
specGateDimensions.rationale: C strings must be null-terminated. Copying character-by-character without writing `\0` leads to garbage printing or memory reads.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the function respect the `max_fields` and 100-character field size limits to prevent array index out of bounds?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Verifies memory bounds checking, which is a crucial habit in C programming to prevent memory corruption.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student uses `strtok` with comma delimiter, which incorrectly splits fields containing commas inside double quotes.
Student forgets to null-terminate individual fields, leading to combined or garbage strings in output.
Student overflows the `fields` array when the CSV line has more elements than `max_fields`.
Student implements the parsing using a pointer `char *p` moving through the string instead of array indexing, which is standard C style.
Student strips double quotes from the output fields even when the spec didn't request quote stripping.
